name: YAML event-stream parser
description:
yaml_parser_parse drives libyaml's streaming event parser: it pulls tokens from the scanner (which itself reads raw, attacker-controlled bytes from a string/file/custom handler) and runs a hand-written recursive-descent state machine (yaml_parser_state_machine) that walks the YAML grammar (stream -> documents -> directives -> block/flow nodes -> sequences/mappings -> scalars/aliases), producing one yaml_event_t per call. Because the scanner/parser directly tokenizes and interprets untrusted bytes (quoting, indentation, escape sequences, directives, anchors/aliases, flow vs. block collections), this is the main attack surface of libyaml and the natural target for a fuzzer that mutates YAML text.
- yaml_parser_parse: target; repeatedly called in a loop until YAML_STREAM_END_EVENT or an error, dispatching into yaml_parser_state_machine which calls the state functions (yaml_parser_parse_document_start/content/end, yaml_parser_parse_node, block/flow sequence and mapping handlers) — this is the core grammar engine.
- yaml_parser_initialize: lifecycle setup required before any parsing call (sets up internal buffers/stacks the state machine and scanner rely on).
- yaml_parser_set_input_string / yaml_parser_set_input_file / yaml_parser_set_input: sources — they feed the raw byte buffer (fuzz input) into the parser's reader, which the scanner (yaml_parser_update_buffer, yaml_parser_fetch_more_tokens/yaml_parser_fetch_next_token) consumes; set_input installs a custom read handler, the other two select string vs. FILE* source, exercising different reader code paths.
- yaml_parser_set_encoding: configuration — forces UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE decoding instead of autodetection via BOM, selecting different branches in the reader's encoding-detection/decoding logic that feeds the scanner.
- yaml_parser_scan: variant — lower-level tokenizer entry point (yaml_parser_fetch_more_tokens/yaml_parser_fetch_next_token and the per-token fetchers like fetch_block_scalar, fetch_flow_scalar, fetch_anchor, fetch_tag, fetch_directive) that yaml_parser_parse itself calls internally; exercising it directly stresses the same scanner core with simpler call discipline.
- yaml_parser_load: consumer/variant — builds a full yaml_document_t tree by repeatedly calling yaml_parser_parse and composing the resulting events (yaml_parser_load_nodes/_document/_alias/_scalar/_sequence/_mapping), adding alias/anchor resolution (yaml_parser_register_anchor) on top of the event stream, exercising more of the feature end-to-end.
- yaml_event_delete: lifecycle cleanup needed after each yaml_parser_parse call to free event-owned buffers (anchors, tags, scalar values) before reuse, required for correct repeated-call protocol (P2).
Input space the harness should vary: the raw YAML document bytes themselves (directives like %YAML/%TAG, anchors `&`/aliases `*`, block vs. flow collections `[]`/`{}`/indentation, single/double/plain/literal/folded scalars, comments, BOM), the chosen input source (string vs. FILE vs. custom read handler), the encoding passed to yaml_parser_set_encoding (YAML_ANY_ENCODING, YAML_UTF8_ENCODING, YAML_UTF16LE_ENCODING, YAML_UTF16BE_ENCODING), and the max nesting level via yaml_set_max_nest_level which bounds the block/flow nesting depth the state machine accepts before erroring.
